CD7D6470DFE60131973F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the technologies responsible for revolutionizing information processing and communications (e.g., computers, cellular phones, Internet).

CD7CFAE0DFE60131973E68A86D17958E.description: Examine the role of scientific knowledge in decisions (e.g., space exploration, what to eat, preventive medicine and medical treatment).

CD7CA3C0DFE60131973D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific discoveries and inventions have changed individuals and societies.

CD7C4F90DFE60131973C68A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific discoveries, inventions, practices, and knowledge influence, and are influenced by, individuals and societies.

CD793150DFE60131973268A86D17958E.description:
Understand the history of Earth and how information about it comes from layers of sedimentary rock, including:
  • sediments and fossils as a record of a very slowly changing world
  • evidence of asteroid impact, volcanic and glacial activity.

CD78E850DFE60131973168A86D17958E.description:
Know that landforms are created and change through a combination of constructive and destructive forces, including:
  • weathering of rock and soil, transportation, deposition of sediment, and tectonic activity
  • similarities and differences between current and past processes on Earth's surface (e.g., erosion, plate tectonics, changes in atmospheric composition)
  • impact of volcanoes and faults on New Mexico geology.

CD7A5740DFE60131973668A86D17958E.description: Understand how to use weather maps and data (e.g., barometric pressure, wind speeds, humidity) to predict weather.

CD7A0C40DFE60131973568A86D17958E.description:
Understand factors that create and influence weather and climate, including:
  • heat, air movement, pressure, humidity, oceans
  • how clouds form by condensation of water vapor
  • how weather patterns are related to atmospheric pressure
  • global patterns of atmospheric movement (e.g., El Niño)
  • factors that can impact Earth's climate (e.g., volcanic eruptions, impacts of asteroids, glaciers).

CD79BB90DFE60131973468A86D17958E.description: Describe the composition (i.e., nitrogen, oxygen, water vapor) and strata of Earth's atmosphere, and differences between the atmosphere of Earth and those of other planets.

CD7BB640DFE60131973A68A86D17958E.description: Know that sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks contain evidence of the materials, temperatures, and forces that created them.

CD7B5F80DFE60131973968A86D17958E.description: Know that Earth's crust is divided into plates that move very slowly, in response to movements in the mantle.

CD7AFD80DFE60131973868A86D17958E.description: Know that Earth is composed of layers that include a crust, mantle, and core.

CD785090DFE60131972F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the structure of Earth and its atmosphere and explain how energy, matter, and forces shape Earth's systems.

CD774BC0DFE60131972C68A86D17958E.description:
Know that the regular and predictable motions of the Earth-moon-sun system explain phenomena on Earth, including:
  • Earth's motion in relation to a year, a day, the seasons, the phases of the moon, eclipses, tides, and shadows
  • moon's orbit around Earth once in 28 days in relation to the phases of the moon.

CD770780DFE60131972B68A86D17958E.description:
Identify the components of the solar system, and describe their defining characteristics and motions in space, including:
  • sun as a medium sized star
  • sun's composition (i.e., hydrogen, helium) and energy production
  • nine planets, their moons, asteroids.

CD76BF50DFE60131972A68A86D17958E.description: Locate the solar system in the Milky Way galaxy.

CD77EB30DFE60131972E68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the objects in the universe, including:
  • billions of galaxies, each containing billions of stars
  • different sizes, temperatures, and colors of stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

CD762990DFE60131972868A86D17958E.description: Describe how the concepts of energy, matter, and force can be used to explain the observed behavior of the solar system, the universe, and their structures.

CD75E1F0DFE60131972768A86D17958E.description: (Earth and Space Science): Understand the structure of Earth, the solar system, and the universe, the interconnections among them, and the processes and interactions of Earth's systems.

CD759CA0DFE60131972668A86D17958E.description: Describe the differences between substances that were produced by living organisms (e.g., fossil fuels) and substances that result from nonliving processes (e.g., igneous rocks).

CD754A90DFE60131972568A86D17958E.description: Explain how fossil fuels were formed from animal and plant cells.

CD74EC30DFE60131972468A86D17958E.description: Understand the structure of organisms and the function of cells in living systems.

CD749E10DFE60131972368A86D17958E.description: Describe how species have responded to changing environmental conditions over time (e.g., extinction, adaptation).

CD7459E0DFE60131972268A86D17958E.description: Understand that the fossil record provides data for how living organisms have evolved.

CD741590DFE60131972168A86D17958E.description: Understand how traits are passed from one generation to the next and how species evolve.

CD73D210DFE60131972068A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms have adapted to various environmental conditions.

CD738B10DFE60131971F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how weather and geologic events (e.g., volcanoes, earthquakes) affect the function of living systems.

CD734010DFE60131971E68A86D17958E.description: Understand how organisms interact with their physical environments to meet their needs (i.e., food, water, air) and how the water cycle is essential to most living systems.

CD72DFF0DFE60131971D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the diverse structures and functions of living things and the complex relationships between living things and their environments.

CD729460DFE60131971C68A86D17958E.description: (Life Science): Understand the properties, structures, and processes of living things and the interdependence of living things and their environments.

CD7243F0DFE60131971B68A86D17958E.description: Know that gravitational force is hard to detect unless one of the objects (e.g., Earth) has a lot of mass.

CD71FEB0DFE60131971A68A86D17958E.description: Know that every object exerts gravitational force on every other object dependent on the masses and distance of separation (e.g., motions of celestial objects, tides).

CD71BBB0DFE60131971968A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain forces that produce motion in objects.

CD717360DFE60131971868A86D17958E.description:
Understand that some energy travels as waves (e.g., seismic, light, sound), including:
  • the sun as source of energy for many processes on Earth
  • different wavelengths of sunlight (e.g., visible, ultraviolet, infrared)
  • vibrations of matter (e.g., sound, earthquakes)
  • different speeds through different materials.

CD712350DFE60131971768A86D17958E.description: Know that there are many forms of energy transfer but that the total amount of energy is conserved (i.e., that energy is neither created nor destroyed).

CD70DFD0DFE60131971668A86D17958E.description: Understand that heat energy can be transferred through conduction, radiation and convection.

CD7098A0DFE60131971568A86D17958E.description: Identify various types of energy (e.g., heat, light, mechanical, electrical, chemical, nuclear).

CD704EE0DFE60131971468A86D17958E.description: Explain the physical processes involved in the transfer, change, and conservation of energy.

CD700480DFE60131971368A86D17958E.description: Know the differences between chemical and physical properties and how these properties can influence the interactions of matter.

CD6FA430DFE60131971268A86D17958E.description: Know that there are about 100 known elements that combine to produce compounds in living organisms and nonliving substances.

CD6F58E0DFE60131971168A86D17958E.description: Use properties to identify substances (e.g., for minerals: the hardness, streak, color, reactivity to acid, cleavage, fracture).

CD6F19F0DFE60131971068A86D17958E.description: Understand that substances have characteristic properties and identify the properties of various substances (e.g., density, boiling point, solubility, chemical reactivity).

CD6EDA10DFE60131970F68A86D17958E.description: Know the forms and properties of matter and how matter interacts.

CD6E9900DFE60131970E68A86D17958E.description: (Physical Science): Understand the structure and properties of matter, the characteristics of energy, and the interactions between matter and energy.

CD6E0E70DFE60131970C68A86D17958E.description: Use probabilities, patterns, and relationships to explain data and observations.

CD6DCB10DFE60131970B68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the usefulness and relevance of data to an investigation.

CD6D8BA0DFE60131970A68A86D17958E.description: Students will use mathematical ideas, tools, and techniques to understand scientific knowledge.

CD6D4AD0DFE60131970968A86D17958E.description: Understand that not all investigations result in defensible scientific explanations.

CD6D0960DFE60131970868A86D17958E.description: Understand that scientific investigations use common processes that include the collection of relevant data and observations, accurate measurements, the identification and control of variables, and logical reasoning to formulate hypotheses and explanations.

CD6CAF60DFE60131970768A86D17958E.description: Understand that scientific knowledge is continually reviewed, critiqued, and revised as new data become available.

CD6C5920DFE60131970668A86D17958E.description: Students will understand the processes of scientific investigation and how scientific inquiry results in scientific knowledge.

CD6C03F0DFE60131970568A86D17958E.description: Justify predictions and conclusions based on data.

CD6BB170DFE60131970468A86D17958E.description: Examine the reasonableness of data supporting a proposed scientific explanation.

CD6B6650DFE60131970368A86D17958E.description: Construct appropriate graphs from data and develop qualitative and quantitative statements about the relationships between variables being investigated.

CD6B1D40DFE60131970268A86D17958E.description: Students will use scientific methods to develop questions, design and conduct experiments using appropriate technologies, analyze and evaluate results, make predictions, and communicate findings.

CD6AD110DFE60131970168A86D17958E.description: Understand the processes of scientific investigations and use inquiry and scientific ways of observing, experimenting, predicting, and validating to think critically.

document.title: Social Studies K-4 Content Standards with Benchmarks and Performance Standards

C9714190DFE601318F0D68A86D17958E.description: Describe trade (e.g., buying and selling, bartering, simple exchange).

C970FFB0DFE601318F0C68A86D17958E.description: Understand the patterns and results of trade and exchange among individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies, and their interdependent qualities.

C9706760DFE601318F0A68A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of product (something produced by human, mechanical, or natural process).

C97026A0DFE601318F0968A86D17958E.description: Understand that economic systems impact the way individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies make decisions about goods and services.

C96FE5D0DFE601318F0868A86D17958E.description: Understand that basic human needs are met in many ways.

C96FA2E0DFE601318F0768A86D17958E.description: Understand that individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies make decisions that affect the distribution of resources and that these decisions are influenced by incentives (both economic and intrinsic).

C96F5C20DFE601318F0668A86D17958E.description: Students understand basic economic principles and use economic reasoning skills to analyze the impact of economic systems (including the market economy) on individuals, families, businesses, communities, and governments.

C96E2230DFE601318F0268A86D17958E.description:
Explain what is meant by "good citizenship," to include:
  1. taking turns and sharing
  2. taking responsibility for own actions, assignments, and personal belongings within the classroom and respecting the property of others.

C96DDFB0DFE601318F0168A86D17958E.description: Describe what is meant by citizenship.

C96D92B0DFE601318F0068A86D17958E.description: Understand rights and responsibilities of "good citizenship" as members of a family, school and community.

C96EBA00DFE601318F0468A86D17958E.description: Describe and provide examples of fairness.

C96E6CA0DFE601318F0368A86D17958E.description: Become familiar with the basic purposes of government in New Mexico and the United States.

C96D3300DFE601318EFF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize patriotic activities including The Pledge of Allegiance, The Star Spangled Banner, salute to the New Mexico flag, and New Mexico state songs.

C96CE0B0DFE601318EFE68A86D17958E.description:
Recognize and name symbols and activities of the United States, New Mexico, and tribes, to include:
  1. United States symbols to include the flag, bald eagle, monuments
  2. New Mexico symbols to include the flag, Smokey Bear, State Bird, chili
  3. tribal symbols and activities to include Feast Days, pottery, arts, storytelling.

C96C9D00DFE601318EFD68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the symbols, icons, songs, traditions, and leaders of local, state, tribal, and national levels that exemplify ideals and provide continuity and a sense of community across time.

C96C57F0DFE601318EFC68A86D17958E.description: Identify authority figures and describe their roles (e.g., parents, teachers, principal, superintendent, police, public officials).

C96C17D0DFE601318EFB68A86D17958E.description: Know the fundamental purposes, concepts, structures, and functions of local, state, tribal, and national governments.

C96BD4D0DFE601318EFA68A86D17958E.description: Students understand the ideals, rights, and responsibilities of citizenship and understand the content and history of the founding documents of the United States with particular emphasis on the United States and New Mexico constitutions and how governments function at local, state, tribal, and national levels.

C96A38A0DFE601318EF468A86D17958E.description: Describe how natural and man-made changes affect the meaning, use, distribution, and value of resources.

C9698E70DFE601318EF268A86D17958E.description: Describe how economic, political, cultural, and social processes interact to shape patterns of human populations, and their interdependence, cooperation, and conflict.

C9687A50DFE601318EEE68A86D17958E.description: Understand how physical processes shape the Earth's surface patterns and biosystems.

C96776E0DFE601318EEB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the natural characteristics of places (e.g., landforms, bodies of water, natural resources, and weather).

C9673090DFE601318EEA68A86D17958E.description: Identify family customs and traditions and explain their importance.

C966EE70DFE601318EE968A86D17958E.description: Be familiar with aspects of human behavior and man-made and natural environments in order to recognize their impact on the past and present.

C966ADB0DFE601318EE868A86D17958E.description: Identify natural characteristics of places (e.g., climate, topography).

C9666BF0DFE601318EE768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between natural and human characteristics of places and use this knowledge to define regions, their relationships with other regions, and patterns of change.

C9661F90DFE601318EE668A86D17958E.description: Define personal direction of front, back, left, and right.

C965D000DFE601318EE568A86D17958E.description: Define relative location of items in the physical environment in terms of over, under, near, far, up, and down.

C9658E00DFE601318EE468A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of location by using and constructing maps, globes, and other geographic tools to identify and derive information about people, places, and environments.

C9654FC0DFE601318EE368A86D17958E.description: Students understand how physical, natural, and cultural processes influence where people live, the ways in which people live, and how societies interact with one another and their environments.

C964D700DFE601318EE168A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of past and present.

C9649940DFE601318EE068A86D17958E.description: Skills: Understand time passage and chronology.

C9645820DFE601318EDF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the local, state, and national symbols (e.g., flag, bird, song).

C963FE90DFE601318EDE68A86D17958E.description: World: Students will identify and describe similar historical characteristics of the United States and its neighboring countries.

C963C100DFE601318EDD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an awareness of community leaders.

C9638010DFE601318EDC68A86D17958E.description: United States: Understand connections among historical events, people, and symbols significant to United States history and cultures.

C9634000DFE601318EDB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the customs, celebrations, and holidays of various cultures in New Mexico.

C962F500DFE601318EDA68A86D17958E.description: New Mexico: Describe how contemporary and historical people and events have influenced New Mexico communities and regions.

C962AE30DFE601318ED968A86D17958E.description: Students are able to identify important people and events in order to analyze significant patterns, relationships, themes, ideas, beliefs, and turning points in New Mexico, United States, and world history in order to understand the complexity of the human experience.

document.title: Physical Education 9-12 Content Standards with Benchmarks and Performance Standards

CE811260DFE60131998A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the physical, social and psychological benefits of a healthy and active lifestyle.

CE80C5C0DFE60131998968A86D17958E.description: Experience the feeling of satisfaction about personal fitness accomplishments; and

CE807010DFE60131998868A86D17958E.description: Create self rewards for achieving personal fitness goals;

CE8023A0DFE60131998768A86D17958E.description: Reflect on reasons for choosing to participate in selected physical activity;

CE7FE1D0DFE60131998668A86D17958E.description: Recognize the feelings that result from physical activity participation:

CE7F9FD0DFE60131998568A86D17958E.description: Create a time management plan to facilitate regular physical activity participation.

CE7F5BA0DFE60131998468A86D17958E.description: Identify barriers and enablers to regular physical activity specific to his or her situation; and

CE7F0FB0DFE60131998368A86D17958E.description: Analyze time, cost and accessibility factors related to regular participation in physical activities:

CE7EADA0DFE60131998268A86D17958E.description: Recognize the connections with lifestyle choices regarding activity and nutrition and the impact on health.

CE7E60F0DFE60131998168A86D17958E.description: Identify key reasons to develop and maintain physical activity and healthy eating habits; and

CE7E1D00DFE60131998068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the importance of physical activity and healthy nutrition as part of one's lifestyle:

CE7DDD40DFE60131997F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize intrinsic value of physical activity.

CE7D9B90DFE60131997E68A86D17958E.description: Choose activities outside of school that provide challenges and social interaction; and

CE7D5950DFE60131997D68A86D17958E.description: Identify activities that best fit their individual needs;

CE7D1190DFE60131997C68A86D17958E.description: Select activities that are enjoyable and promote fitness;

CE7CC490DFE60131997B68A86D17958E.description: Maintain and improve physical fitness, motor skills and knowledge about physical activity:

CE7C7590DFE60131997A68A86D17958E.description: Understands that physical activity provides opportunities for enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and social interaction. Students will:

CE7C0D30DFE60131997968A86D17958E.description: Critically analyze advertising messages; create print ads endorsing healthy lifestyles.

CE7BB4F0DFE60131997868A86D17958E.description: Know that billboards, magazines and television will show idealistic body types; and

CE7B63D0DFE60131997768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that media messages are trying to sell products;

CE7B1970DFE60131997668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how the media, particularly advertising, influence the perception of the ideal body types:

CE7AD570DFE60131997568A86D17958E.description: Display a sensitive attitude and a willingness to participate with others in physical activities.

CE7A9190DFE60131997468A86D17958E.description: Recognize the importance of working cooperatively with persons of diverse backgrounds and abilities during any activity; and

CE7A4C90DFE60131997368A86D17958E.description: Develop strategies for including persons of diverse backgrounds and abilities in physical activity:

CE79F9C0DFE60131997268A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge the attributes that individuals with differences bring to a group.

CE79AB40DFE60131997168A86D17958E.description: Discuss why social differences and other aspects keep young adults from participating in an active lifestyle; and

CE795000DFE60131997068A86D17958E.description: Identify the effects of age, gender, race, ethnicity, socioeconomic standing and culture upon physical activity choices and participation:

CE790B40DFE60131996F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates understanding and respect for differences among people in physical activity settings. Students will:

CE78C440DFE60131996E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between group member roles (e.g. leader, follower, etc.) and act accordingly to accomplish group goals.

CE787F60DFE60131996D68A86D17958E.description: Accept leadership responsibility and a willingness to follow, as appropriate, in order to accomplish group goals:

CE783B30DFE60131996C68A86D17958E.description: Openly discuss conflicts with the teacher and others involved while using conflict resolution skills.

CE77F360DFE60131996B68A86D17958E.description: Accept consequences of personal choices; and

CE77A490DFE60131996A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to make responsible decisions regardless of peer pressure;

CE775FB0DFE60131996968A86D17958E.description: Recognize the influence of peer pressure and exhibit appropriate strategies for conflict resolution;

CE7719D0DFE60131996868A86D17958E.description: Follow general classroom and specific activity rules to insure physical and emotional safety.

CE76C9C0DFE60131996768A86D17958E.description: Initiate independent and responsible personal behavior in physical activity settings:

CE767FC0DFE60131996668A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate etiquette in all activities.

CE763920DFE60131996568A86D17958E.description: Adhere to the general classroom and specific activity rules as well as assisting with the care of the equipment and facilities; and

CE75E980DFE60131996468A86D17958E.description: Identify and evaluate risks and safety factors that may affect physical activity choices throughout the life cycle:

CE75A320DFE60131996368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. Students will:

CE755FC0DFE60131996268A86D17958E.description: Create a scientifically-based personal fitness program that encompasses cardiovascular, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition principles in the fitness plan.

CE751B90DFE60131996168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a knowledge base on training principles (i.e., progression, overload, specificity, etc.); and

CE74D7B0DFE60131996068A86D17958E.description: Provide rationale for the principles of frequency, intensity, time and type;

CE749190DFE60131995F68A86D17958E.description: Provide rationale for the use of scientific concepts in the development of one's fitness program;

CE743F40DFE60131995E68A86D17958E.description: Design personal fitness programs that encompass all health-related physical fitness components:

CE73F080DFE60131995D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability and knowledge to self-assess health-related fitness levels (i.e., resting heart rate, recovery heart rate, target heart rate, heart rate zone, muscular strength, endurance, flexibility, body composition, etc.) based upon health-related fitness criteria (i.e., develop strategies for achieving and maintaining a personal fitness program).

CE73AF40DFE60131995C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate independence in assessing, achieving and maintaining personal health-related fitness goals:

CE736E30DFE60131995B68A86D17958E.description: Maintain a personal fitness program by using exercise strategies (i.e., goal statements, graphs, charts, software, log books, etc.).

CE732C30DFE60131995A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the importance of participation in physical activity on a regular basis:

CE72E7D0DFE60131995968A86D17958E.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of physical fitness. Students will:

CE729C70DFE60131995868A86D17958E.description: Analyze different physical activities to determine a well-balanced health-related fitness program to help enhance overall fitness (i.e., cardiovascular, muscular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility activities, etc.).

document.title: Science Content Standards, Benchmarks, and Performance Standards

CD5AEFC0DFE6013196FE68A86D17958E.description: Describe how various technologies have affected the lives of individuals (e.g., transportation, entertainment, health).

CD5AAD20DFE6013196FD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the contributions of science to understanding local or current issues (e.g., watershed and community decisions regarding water use).

CD5A6660DFE6013196FC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific discoveries and inventions have changed individuals and societies.

CD5A16F0DFE6013196FB68A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific discoveries, inventions, practices, and knowledge influence, and are influenced by, individuals and societies.

CD5983A0DFE6013196F968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the seasons are caused by Earth's motion around the sun and the tilt of Earth's axis of rotation.

CD593250DFE6013196F868A86D17958E.description: Know that most of Earth's surface is covered by water, that most of that water is salt water in oceans, and that fresh water is found in rivers, lakes, underground sources, and glaciers.

CD58EAF0DFE6013196F768A86D17958E.description: Know that air is a substance that surrounds Earth (atmosphere), takes up space, and moves, and that temperature fluctuations and other factors produce wind currents.

CD58A1E0DFE6013196F668A86D17958E.description:
Understand that water and air relate to Earth's processes, including:
  • how the water cycle relates to weather
  • how clouds are made of tiny droplets of water, like fog or steam.

CD5852A0DFE6013196F568A86D17958E.description: Describe the structure of Earth and its atmosphere and explain how energy, matter, and forces shape Earth's systems.

CD581290DFE6013196F468A86D17958E.description: Know that there have been manned and unmanned journeys to space and to the moon.

CD57D0E0DFE6013196F368A86D17958E.description: Understand that Earth is part of a larger solar system, which is part of an even larger galaxy (Milky Way), which is one of many galaxies.

CD578C40DFE6013196F268A86D17958E.description: Know that many objects in the universe are huge and are separated from one another by vast distances (e.g., many stars are larger than the sun but so distant that they look like points of light).

CD574AC0DFE6013196F168A86D17958E.description: Describe how the concepts of energy, matter, and force can be used to explain the observed behavior of the solar system, the universe, and their structures.

CD5706D0DFE6013196F068A86D17958E.description: (Earth and Space Science): Understand the structure of Earth, the solar system, and the universe, the interconnections among them, and the processes and interactions of Earth's systems.

CD56AF30DFE6013196EF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationships among cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, whole organisms, and ecosystems.

CD566270DFE6013196EE68A86D17958E.description: Know that some organisms are made of a collection of similar cells that cooperate (e.g., algae) while other organisms are made of cells that are different in appearance and function (e.g., corn, birds).

CD5617A0DFE6013196ED68A86D17958E.description: Understand that all living organisms are composed of cells from one to many trillions, and that cells are usually only visible through a microscope.

CD55D4E0DFE6013196EC68A86D17958E.description: Understand the structure of organisms and the function of cells in living systems.

CD559140DFE6013196EB68A86D17958E.description: Understand that heredity is the process by which traits are passed from one generation to another.

CD554B30DFE6013196EA68A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics of an organism that are inherited from its parents (e.g., eye color in humans, flower color in plants) and other characteristics that are learned or result from interactions with the environment.

CD54FFF0DFE6013196E968A86D17958E.description: Know that plants and animals have life cycles that include birth, growth and development, reproduction, and death and that these cycles differ for different organisms.

CD54B9D0DFE6013196E868A86D17958E.description: Understand how traits are passed from one generation to the next and how species evolve.

CD547790DFE6013196E768A86D17958E.description: Describe how human activity impacts the environment.

CD53EC60DFE6013196E568A86D17958E.description: Understand how food webs depict relationships between different organisms.

CD539ED0DFE6013196E468A86D17958E.description: Identify the components of habitats and ecosystems (producers, consumers, decomposers, predators).

CD5148F0DFE6013196DC68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain forces that produce motion in objects.

CD4FF470DFE6013196D768A86D17958E.description: Explain the physical processes involved in the transfer, change, and conservation of energy.

CD4D6E20DFE6013196CF68A86D17958E.description: (Physical Science): Understand the structure and properties of matter, the characteristics of energy, and the interactions between matter and energy.
