CE61A470DFE60131993E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe personal feelings resulting from participation in physical activity (i.e., journals, activity calendars, peer mentoring, class discussions, etc.); and

CE615230DFE60131993D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate aesthetic appreciation of skilled movement of the body (i.e., create body silhouettes, etc.);

CE60F020DFE60131993C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and use a variety of physical activities and movements to communicate ideas and feelings (i.e., dance, sports, gymnastics, intensity levels, etc.);

CE609B30DFE60131993B68A86D17958E.description: Practice and demonstrate physical activity as a vehicle for self expression:

CE6052F0DFE60131993A68A86D17958E.description: Sharing feelings of satisfaction felt as a result of physical activity (i.e., improved individual self-esteem, good feelings gained from being part of a team, activity journals, class discussions, etc.).

CE5FFF30DFE60131993968A86D17958E.description: Appreciate the challenging aspects of competition with self and others (i.e., praise opponents, accept teammates' and opponents' contributions, enjoy physical activity for its own sake, etc.); and

CE5FB900DFE60131993868A86D17958E.description: Identify basic ideals of fair play, acceptance of rules and group communication (i.e., give appropriate feedback to partners and teammates, etc.);

CE5F7250DFE60131993768A86D17958E.description: Identify the social benefits of participation in physical activity; grades 5-8 performance standards:

CE5F2840DFE60131993668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a willingness to try an unfamiliar position within the context of a practice or a game situation (i.e., offense versus defense, guard versus forward, catcher versus pitcher, etc.).

CE5ED4E0DFE60131993568A86D17958E.description: Develop a matrix of available school and community physical activity resources; and

CE5E9020DFE60131993468A86D17958E.description: Participate in new and challenging physical activities:

CE5E4840DFE60131993368A86D17958E.description: Show a desire to improve one's own physical ability, fitness level and performance (i.e., fitness journals, activity calendars, fitness level assessments, etc).

CE5DF2C0DFE60131993268A86D17958E.description: Identify benefits of participating in physical activities throughout one's lifetime (i.e., discussion, lists, outline, role playing, etc.); and

CE5DA1A0DFE60131993168A86D17958E.description: Choose to participate consistently in games, sports, dance and outdoor activities, both in and out of school, based on individual interests and capabilities (i.e., at school during self-selection times, after-school free time, teams, lessons, family recreation, etc.);

CE5D4C80DFE60131993068A86D17958E.description: Identify a variety of physical activities that will provide satisfaction and lead to continued participation;

CE5CA960DFE60131992E68A86D17958E.description: Understands that physical activity provides opportunities for enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and social interaction. Students will:

CE5C6650DFE60131992D68A86D17958E.description: Produce a media advertisement that promotes the benefits of an active and healthy lifestyle.

CE5C2120DFE60131992C68A86D17958E.description: Describe differences between healthy bodies and media-generated bodies; and

CE5BD460DFE60131992B68A86D17958E.description: Explain/describe how media influences our consumer choices and personal/physical self-concept;

CE5B6F90DFE60131992A68A86D17958E.description: Initiate discussion of media influences on behavior choices (i.e., print, radio, TV, etc.);

CE5B1620DFE60131992968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the media, particularly advertising, influences the perception of ideal body types:

CE5AD300DFE60131992868A86D17958E.description: Describe the social dynamics that occur when peers participate with partners in cooperative activities.

CE5A8EF0DFE60131992768A86D17958E.description: Participate in games/activities in which handicapping conditions are simulated (i.e., wheelchair basketball, etc.); and

CE5A4860DFE60131992668A86D17958E.description: Recognize the diverse attributes of age, race, ethnicity, gender and ability level and acknowledge how these differences can enhance group activities;

CE5A0390DFE60131992568A86D17958E.description: Understand the need for game modifications to allow persons with special needs to participate;

CE59B8B0DFE60131992468A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge all people of different gender, culture, ethnicity and disability and seek to learn more about both similarities and differences:

CE596900DFE60131992368A86D17958E.description: Research and present an unfamiliar game or dance from another country.

CE591D90DFE60131992268A86D17958E.description: Describe why "I" (student) participate in certain sports/dance/activities based on my culture; and

CE58C9C0DFE60131992168A86D17958E.description: Describe why certain sports/dances/activities are more prevalent in specific countries/cultures;

CE5876B0DFE60131992068A86D17958E.description: Identify the contribution that physical activity plays in multicultural/ethnic awareness and in the acceptance of all peers:

CE5824C0DFE60131991F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates understanding and respect for differences among people in physical activity settings. Students will:

CE57DB20DFE60131991E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze cause and effect during physical activities.

CE577BA0DFE60131991D68A86D17958E.description: Explain what it means to be a good team player; and

CE5735B0DFE60131991C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate importance of positive attitudes (i.e., communication, body language and listening skills, etc.);

CE56EFF0DFE60131991B68A86D17958E.description: Explain different styles of leadership skills;

CE5660C0DFE60131991968A86D17958E.description: Participate positively in team building/cooperative activities;

CE559D90DFE60131991768A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with a group to achieve group goals:

CE554540DFE60131991668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ability to apply concepts of good sportsmanship (i.e., as participant, as spectator, as referee, as coach, etc.).

CE5503E0DFE60131991568A86D17958E.description: Identify and list components of sportsmanship (i.e., differentiate between positive and negative sportsmanship, fair play, respect referee's decision, understand importance of following rules, adhere to good sportsmanship concepts/ideas, etc.); and

CE54C1B0DFE60131991468A86D17958E.description: When in conflict, use appropriate problem-solving techniques (i.e., conflict mediation, cooperative discipline techniques, small group discussion/processing, etc.);

CE547E90DFE60131991368A86D17958E.description: List coping skills for dealing with negative behaviors (i.e., bully proofing, sexual harassment awareness, peer mediation, conflict resolution, etc.);

CE543A70DFE60131991268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and ignore poor behavior choices of peers (i.e., identify bullying behaviors, identify sexual harassment behaviors, etc.);

CE53E710DFE60131991168A86D17958E.description: Identify/make positive choices in a variety of physical education settings (i.e., no teasing, name calling - use positive language, follow physical safety rules, follow all game/activity rules, etc.);

CE53A5C0DFE60131991068A86D17958E.description: Recognize the influence of peer pressure and make appropriate decisions using problem-solving techniques to resolve conflict:

CE536420DFE60131990F68A86D17958E.description: Accept responsibility for own actions and modify behaviors accordingly (i.e., take self out of negative situation, go to a safe adult in an unsafe situation, etc.).

CE532080DFE60131990E68A86D17958E.description: Identify a sexual harassment situation and respond appropriately (i.e., refer to specific district regulations/policies, go to a safe adult when in an unsafe situation, demonstrate use of appropriate language and personal contact during physical activities, etc.); and

CE52DCE0DFE60131990D68A86D17958E.description: Identify a bullying situation and respond appropriately (i.e., refer to specific district "bully proofing" programs/parameters, go to a safe adult when in an unsafe situation, etc.);

CE5297D0DFE60131990C68A86D17958E.description: Exhibit appropriate personal and group conduct while engaging in physical activity:

CE524D90DFE60131990B68A86D17958E.description: Follow established emergency procedures (i.e., first aid, fire drills, etc.); wear appropriate activity attire properly (i.e., shoes and socks, clothing specific to activity, clothing specific to school and district rules, no potentially harmful accessories, etc.).

CE51F920DFE60131990A68A86D17958E.description: Follow general classroom and specific activity rules (i.e., treat each other with respect, honor specific boundaries, use appropriate personal contact, positive response to teachers' instruction/comments, distinguish between compliance and non-compliance with rules and regulations and apply agreed-upon consequences when officiating, etc.); and

CE51B100DFE60131990968A86D17958E.description: Use equipment appropriately (i.e., use specific equipment for intended purposes, proper care and management of equipment, etc.);

CE5168B0DFE60131990868A86D17958E.description: Select and utilize safety principles in physical activity settings; grades 5-8 performance standards:

CE511600DFE60131990768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. Students will:

CE50C630DFE60131990668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effectiveness of current fitness programs and revise physical fitness activities to meet fitness goals (i.e., include more aerobic activities, adjust sets and reps in strength programs, etc.).

CE506FC0DFE60131990568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of exercise and other factors to obtain personal fitness goals:

CE49D450DFE60131990468A86D17958E.description: Generate an appropriate physical fitness plan to maintain and or improve strengths and weaknesses.

CE497320DFE60131990368A86D17958E.description: Analyze personal fitness data and evaluate individual strengths and weaknesses; and

CE492840DFE60131990268A86D17958E.description: Interpret the results of physical fitness assessments and use this information to develop individualized physical fitness goals with guidance from the teacher:

CE48DA30DFE60131990168A86D17958E.description: Analyze personal fitness data and evaluate individual strengths and weaknesses.

CE4874B0DFE60131990068A86D17958E.description: Assess personal fitness status within each health-related physical fitness component:

CE47B820DFE6013198FE68A86D17958E.description: Identify the benefits of a healthy body composition versus the risks of an unhealthy body composition.

CE469AE0DFE6013198FA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and identify fitness activities that require muscular strength and muscular endurance;

CE45D090DFE6013198F868A86D17958E.description: Analyze appropriate physical activities that result in the development of cardiovascular endurances;

CE481280DFE6013198FF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the benefits of a healthy body composition.

CE472F40DFE6013198FC68A86D17958E.description: Comprehend the benefits of flexibility; and

CE46E8C0DFE6013198FB68A86D17958E.description: Select appropriate fitness activities that require muscular strength and muscular endurance;

CE462ED0DFE6013198F968A86D17958E.description: Engage in appropriate physical activity that results in the development of cardiovascular endurance;

CE4588D0DFE6013198F768A86D17958E.description: Participate in physical activities that address each health-related physical fitness component:

CE454070DFE6013198F668A86D17958E.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of physical fitness. Students will:

CE44F6F0DFE6013198F568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the difference between aerobic and anaerobic fitness activities.

CE44A6A0DFE6013198F468A86D17958E.description: Outline the health risk factors associated with an inactive lifestyle versus an active lifestyle, etc.); and

CE444AB0DFE6013198F368A86D17958E.description: Analyze and illustrate the benefits of physical activity (i.e., differentiate inactive versus active lifestyles;

CE43FC30DFE6013198F268A86D17958E.description: Determine long-term benefits that may result from regular participation in physical activity:

CE43AAF0DFE6013198F168A86D17958E.description: Choose and record levels of participation in physical activities with the intent to improve and or maintain each of the following components of health-related fitness: muscular strength (i.e., push-ups, thera-bands, weights, pull-ups, tumbling, etc.); endurance (i.e., running, aerobic activities, etc.); flexibility (i.e., stretching/warm-up, cool-down activities, tumbling, etc.); cardiovascular (i.e., running and aerobic activities, etc.); body composition (i.e., toning activities, aerobic/anaerobic activities, weight training, etc.).

CE436680DFE6013198F068A86D17958E.description: Maintain heart rate within the target heart rate zone (i.e., apply personal target heart rate data into an individualized personal physical activity, etc.); and

CE4310C0DFE6013198EF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and interpret personal fitness data in order to establish personal fitness/activity goals;

CE429AE0DFE6013198EE68A86D17958E.description: Be able to set personal physical activity goals and participate in individualized programs of physical activity and exercise:

CE425A10DFE6013198ED68A86D17958E.description: Exhibits knowledge and ability to participate in a physically active lifestyle. Students will:

CE421620DFE6013198EC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ability to analyze a movement pattern by using knowledge of its critical elements (i.e., self-analysis and peer observation, etc.).

CE41D230DFE6013198EB68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of results to correct and improve future performance; and

CE418D50DFE6013198EA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in the use of critical elements of fundamental and specialized movement skills:

CE414760DFE6013198E968A86D17958E.description: Analyze a task to identify movement skills, how they are sequenced and how they are applied to produce a desired outcome.

CE40FAE0DFE6013198E868A86D17958E.description: Detect and correct errors in personal performance, based on knowledge of results, while participating in selected activities; and

CE40A550DFE6013198E768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in the use of motor skills, motor behaviors and motor learning concepts in increasingly complex movement situations:

CE406300DFE6013198E668A86D17958E.description: Describe how spatial relationships with other players affect outcomes during playing situations (i.e., badminton: up and back or side by side position; basketball: one on one or zone; soccer: outcomes of passing and receiving, etc.).

CE402060DFE6013198E568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in the use of the concepts of body, effort, space and relationships in movement:

CE3FDC80DFE6013198E468A86D17958E.description: Applies movement concepts and principles to the learning and development of motor skills. Students will:

CE3F9380DFE6013198E368A86D17958E.description: For dual sports, during game situations, students will reproduce sequences of basic techniques and skills consisting of: foot work, court position, offensive and defensive strokes, placement of projectile and court position in relation to partner.

CE3F49A0DFE6013198E268A86D17958E.description: For team sports, in a game situation, defensive players will show and maintain proper position and techniques while offensive players use practiced plays and deception to move to open space; and

CE3EEE40DFE6013198E168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate proficiency using basic offensive and defensive strategies while playing a modified version of a learned team and individual sport:

CE3E99E0DFE6013198E068A86D17958E.description: Using basic individual activity skills, students will display a combination of skills in response to a variety of activity situations (i.e., tennis: serve, center court, forehand; golf: drive, chip, pitch, putt determined by lay of the ball; wall climbing: "on belay," 3-point contact, climb with legs, stabilize with arms, etc.).

CE3E4830DFE6013198DF68A86D17958E.description: Using basic team sport skills, students will display a combination of skills in response to a variety of game situations (i.e., basketball: receive, pivot, dribble, shoot; soccer: receive, control, dribble, pass/shoot; baseball/softball: batting, base running, sliding, etc.); and

CE3DF750DFE6013198DE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate proficiency in combining basic skills for participating in a variety of physical fitness activities: aquatics, dance, outdoor pursuits, individual activities/sports and team activities/sports:

CE3D9C70DFE6013198DD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates competency in many movement forms and proficiency in a few movement forms. Students will:

document.title: Science Content Standards, Benchmarks, and Performance Standards

CC94C7B0DFE60131964068A86D17958E.description: Know that science has discovered many things about objects, events, and nature and that there are many more questions to be answered.

CC948150DFE60131963F68A86D17958E.description: Understand that everybody can do science, invent things, and formulate ideas.

CC943580DFE60131963E68A86D17958E.description: Know that some materials are better than others for making particular things (e.g., paper, cardboard, plastic, metal, fiberglass, wood).

CC93F100DFE60131963D68A86D17958E.description: Know that science has ways to help living things avoid sickness or recover from sickness (e.g., vaccinations, medicine) and adult supervision is needed to administer them.

CC93AA10DFE60131963C68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways to prevent the spread of germs (e.g., soap, bleach, cooking).

CC9361E0DFE60131963B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how science influences decisions made by individuals and societies.

CC930FB0DFE60131963A68A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific discoveries, inventions, practices, and knowledge influence, and are influenced by, individuals and societies.

CC9262F0DFE60131963868A86D17958E.description: Recognize the characteristics of the seasons.

CC921650DFE60131963768A86D17958E.description: Know that soil is made up of weathered rock and organic materials, and that soils differ in their capacity to support the growth of plants.

CC91C510DFE60131963668A86D17958E.description: Understand that rocks are made of materials with distinct properties.

CC917C70DFE60131963568A86D17958E.description: Know that rocks have different shapes and sizes (e.g., boulders, pebbles, sand) and that smaller rocks result from the breaking and weathering of larger rocks.

CC913860DFE60131963468A86D17958E.description: Know the structure and formation of Earth and its atmosphere and the processes that shape them.

CC90F280DFE60131963368A86D17958E.description: Know that the sun is a star.

CC90A850DFE60131963268A86D17958E.description: Observe that some objects in the night sky are brighter than others.

CC906410DFE60131963168A86D17958E.description: Observe that the phase of the moon appears a little different every day but looks the same again after about four weeks.

CC902100DFE60131963068A86D17958E.description: Know the structure of the solar system and the objects in the universe.

CC8FDBD0DFE60131962F68A86D17958E.description: (Earth and Space Science): Understand the structure of Earth, the solar system, and the universe, the interconnections among them, and the processes and interactions of Earth's systems.

CC8F93C0DFE60131962E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the functions of human systems (e.g., respiratory, circulatory, digestive).

CC8F4DA0DFE60131962D68A86D17958E.description: Know that various nutrients are required for specific parts and functions of the body (e.g., milk for bones and teeth, protein for muscles, sugar for energy).

CC8F0280DFE60131962C68A86D17958E.description: Identify a variety of human organs (e.g., lungs, heart, stomach, brain).

CC8EBEE0DFE60131962B68A86D17958E.description: Know the parts of the human body and their functions.

CC8E7A60DFE60131962A68A86D17958E.description: Observe how the environment influences some characteristics of living things (e.g., amount of sunlight required for plant growth).

CC8E3570DFE60131962968A86D17958E.description: Observe that many characteristics of the offspring of living organisms (e.g., plants or animals) are inherited from their parents.

CC8DF040DFE60131962868A86D17958E.description: Explain that stages of the life cycle are different for different animals (e.g., mouse, cat, horse, butterfly, frog).

CC8DA500DFE60131962768A86D17958E.description: Know that living things have similarities and differences and that living things change over time.

CC8D5890DFE60131962668A86D17958E.description: Know that bacteria and viruses are germs.

CC8D0EA0DFE60131962568A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe various shapes of fungi.

CC8CBCD0DFE60131962468A86D17958E.description: Observe that diversity exists among individuals within a population.

CC8C7D80DFE60131962368A86D17958E.description: Know that living things have diverse forms, structures, functions, and habitats.

CC8C3C30DFE60131962268A86D17958E.description: (Life Science): Understand the properties, structures, and processes of living things and the interdependence of living things and their environments.

CC8BF1D0DFE60131962168A86D17958E.description: Observe that electrically charged materials and magnets attract and repel each other, and observe their effects on other kinds of materials.

CC8BA2B0DFE60131962068A86D17958E.description: Describe how the strength of a push or pull affects the change in an object's motion (e.g., how a big or small push affects how high a swing rises).

CC8B63E0DFE60131961F68A86D17958E.description: Identify forces and describe the motion of objects.

CC8B23B0DFE60131961E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that moving objects carry energy (kinetic energy).

CC8AE070DFE60131961D68A86D17958E.description: Observe that sound is made by vibrating objects and describe it by its pitch and loudness.

CC8A97A0DFE60131961C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the usefulness of some forms of energy (e.g., electricity, sunlight, wind, sound) and how energy (e.g., heat, light,) can affect common objects (e.g., sunlight warms dark objects, heat melts candles).

CC8A4A70DFE60131961B68A86D17958E.description: Know that heat moves more rapidly in thermal conductors (e.g., metal pan) than in insulators (e.g., plastic handle).

CC89F650DFE60131961A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how heat can be produced (e.g., burning, rubbing, mixing some substances).

CC89B6D0DFE60131961968A86D17958E.description: Know that energy is needed to get things done and that energy has different forms.

CC8978F0DFE60131961868A86D17958E.description: Describe the changes that occur when substances are heated or cooled and change from one state of matter to another (i.e., solid, liquid, and gas).

CC893B00DFE60131961768A86D17958E.description: Observe that properties of substances can change when they are mixed, cooled, or heated (e.g., salt dissolves in water, ice melts).

CC88FA50DFE60131961668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that matter has different forms and properties.

CC88B900DFE60131961568A86D17958E.description: (Physical Science): Understand the structure and properties of matter, the characteristics of energy, and the interactions between matter and energy.

CC8826B0DFE60131961368A86D17958E.description: Measure length, weight, and temperature with appropriate tools and express those measurements in accurate mathematical language.

CC87E790DFE60131961268A86D17958E.description: Record observations on simple charts or diagrams.

CC87A940DFE60131961168A86D17958E.description: Students will use mathematical skills and vocabulary to analyze data, understand patterns and relationships, and communicate findings.

CC876B50DFE60131961068A86D17958E.description: Make accurate observations and communicate findings about investigations.

CC872CE0DFE60131960F68A86D17958E.description: Understand that in doing science it is often helpful to work with a team and share findings.

CC86ECA0DFE60131960E68A86D17958E.description: Students will use scientific thinking and knowledge and communicate findings.

CC86A950DFE60131960D68A86D17958E.description: Follow simple instructions for a scientific investigation.

CC865F00DFE60131960C68A86D17958E.description: Make predictions based on observed patterns as opposed to random guessing.

CC861DE0DFE60131960B68A86D17958E.description: Use tools to provide information not directly available through only the senses (e.g., magnifiers, rulers, thermometers).

CC85DA40DFE60131960A68A86D17958E.description: Conduct simple investigations (e.g., measure the sizes of plants of the same kind that are grown in sunlight and in shade).

CC8592D0DFE60131960968A86D17958E.description: Students will use scientific methods to observe, collect, record, analyze, predict, interpret, and determine reasonableness of data.

CC8545C0DFE60131960868A86D17958E.description: Understand the processes of scientific investigations and use inquiry and scientific ways of observing, experimenting, predicting, and validating to think critically.

document.title: Science Content Standards, Benchmarks, and Performance Standards

CE08DDB0DFE60131986D68A86D17958E.description: Know that science plays a role in many different kinds of careers and activities (e.g., public service, volunteers, public office holders, researchers, teachers, doctors, nurses, technicians, farmers, ranchers).

CE088FC0DFE60131986C68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scientists have characteristics in common with other individuals (e.g., employment and career needs, curiosity, desire to perform public service, greed, preconceptions and biases, temptation to be unethical, core values including honesty and openness).

CE0840C0DFE60131986B68A86D17958E.description: Identify important questions that science cannot answer (e.g., questions that are beyond today's science, decisions that science can only help to make, questions that are inherently outside of the realm of science).

CE07F0B0DFE60131986A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that reasonable people may disagree about some issues that are of interest to both science and religion (e.g., the origin of life on Earth, the cause of the Big Bang, the future of Earth).

CE079C00DFE60131986968A86D17958E.description: Identify how science has produced knowledge that is relevant to individual health and material prosperity.

CE0AC590DFE60131987368A86D17958E.description: Describe New Mexico's role in nuclear science (e.g., Manhattan Project, WIPP, national laboratories).

CE0A7CB0DFE60131987268A86D17958E.description: Describe how environmental, economic, and political interests impact resource management and use in New Mexico.

CE0A32A0DFE60131987168A86D17958E.description: Explain how societies can change ecosystems and how these changes can be reversible or irreversible.

CE09E3B0DFE60131987068A86D17958E.description: Know that societal factors can promote or constrain scientific discovery (e.g., government funding, laws and regulations about human cloning and genetically modified organisms, gender and ethnic bias, AIDS research, alternative-energy research).

CE0995C0DFE60131986F68A86D17958E.description: Describe major historical changes in scientific perspectives (e.g., atomic theory, germs, cosmology, relativity, plate tectonics, evolution) and the experimental observations that triggered them.

CE0B22C0DFE60131987468A86D17958E.description: Describe how scientific knowledge helps decision makers with local, national, and global challenges (e.g., Waste Isolation Pilot Project [WIPP], mining, drought, population growth, alternative energy, climate change).

CE0E3E70DFE60131987D68A86D17958E.description: Describe uses of radioactivity (e.g., nuclear power, nuclear medicine, radiometric dating).

CE0DF220DFE60131987C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how human activities have affected ozone in the upper atmosphere and how it affects health and the environment.

CE0DA1B0DFE60131987B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of digital technologies on the availability, creation, and dissemination of information.

CE0D50C0DFE60131987A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that applications of genetics can meet human needs and can create new problems (e.g., agriculture, medicine, cloning).

CE0CFFA0DFE60131987968A86D17958E.description: Understand the scientific foundations of common technologies (e.g., kitchen appliances, radio, television, aircraft, rockets, computers, medical X-rays, selective breeding, fertilizers and pesticides, agricultural equipment).

CE0CAA90DFE60131987868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the influences of technology on society (e.g., communications, petroleum, transportation, nuclear energy, computers, medicine, genetic engineering) including both desired and undesired effects, and including some historical examples (e.g., the wheel, the plow, the printing press, the lightning rod).

CE0C5830DFE60131987768A86D17958E.description: Understand how advances in technology enable further advances in science (e.g., microscopes and cellular structure; telescopes and understanding of the universe).

CE0C0320DFE60131987668A86D17958E.description: Know how science enables technology but also constrains it, and recognize the difference between real technology and science fiction (e.g., rockets vs. antigravity machines; nuclear reactors vs. perpetual-motion machines; medical X-rays vs. Star-Trek tricorders).

CE06E2B0DFE60131986768A86D17958E.description: Examine and analyze how scientific discoveries and their applications affect the world, and explain how societies influence scientific investigations and applications.

CE068A90DFE60131986668A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific discoveries, inventions, practices, and knowledge influence, and are influenced by, individuals and societies.

CE0222B0DFE60131985968A86D17958E.description: Explain how the availability of ground water through aquifers can fluctuate based on multiple factors (i.e., rate of use, rate of replenishment, surface changes, and changes in temperature).

CE01CF00DFE60131985868A86D17958E.description: Explain how layers of the atmosphere (e.g., ozone, ionosphere) change naturally and artificially.

CE017430DFE60131985768A86D17958E.description:
Describe the composition and structure of Earth's materials, including:
  • the major rock types (i.e., sedimentary, igneous, metamorphic) and their formation
  • natural resources (e.g., minerals, petroleum) and their formation.

CE0290A0DFE60131985A68A86D17958E.description: Know that Earth's system contains a fixed amount of natural resources that cycle among land, water, the atmosphere, and living things (e.g., carbon and nitrogen cycles, rock cycle, water cycle, ground water, aquifers).

CE03C9F0DFE60131985E68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the patterns and relationships in the circulation of air and water driven by the sun's radiant energy, including:
  • patterns in weather systems related to the transfer of energy
  • differences between climate and weather
  • global climate, global warming, and the greenhouse effect
  • El Niño, La Niña, and other climatic trends.

CE037CA0DFE60131985D68A86D17958E.description:
Describe convection as the mechanism for moving heat energy from deep within Earth to the surface and discuss how this process results in plate tectonics, including:
  • geological manifestations (e.g., earthquakes, volcanoes, mountain building) that occur at plate boundaries
  • impact of plate motions on societies and the environment (e.g., earthquakes, volcanoes).

CE032FF0DFE60131985C68A86D17958E.description: Know that Earth's systems are driven by internal (i.e., radioactive decay and gravitational energy) and external (i.e., the sun) sources of energy.

CE05DE60DFE60131986468A86D17958E.description: Explain plate tectonic theory and understand the evidence that supports it.

CE0562C0DFE60131986368A86D17958E.description:
Understand the changes in Earth's past and the investigative methods used to determine geologic time, including:
  • rock sequences, relative dating, fossil correlation, and radiometric dating
  • geologic time scales, historic changes in life forms, and the evidence for absolute ages (e.g., radiometric methods, tree rings, paleomagnetism).

CE0515A0DFE60131986268A86D17958E.description: Describe the internal structure of Earth (e.g., core, mantle, crust) and the structure of Earth's plates.

CE04C720DFE60131986168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that radiometric data indicate that Earth is at least 4 billion years old and that Earth has changed during that period.

CE047590DFE60131986068A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics and the evolution of Earth in terms of the geosphere, the hydrosphere, the atmosphere, and the biosphere.

CE00BD90DFE60131985568A86D17958E.description: Examine the scientific theories of the origin, structure, energy, and evolution of Earth and its atmosphere, and their interconnections.

CE006F80DFE60131985468A86D17958E.description: Examine the role that New Mexico research facilities play in current space exploration (e.g., Very Large Array, Goddard Space Center).

CE001430DFE60131985368A86D17958E.description: Describe how stars are powered by nuclear fusion, how luminosity and temperature indicate their age, and how stellar processes create heavier and stable elements that are found throughout the universe.

CDFFB240DFE60131985268A86D17958E.description: Explain how objects in the universe emit different electromagnetic radiation and how this information is used.

CDFF6480DFE60131985168A86D17958E.description: Describe the key observations that led to the acceptance of the Big Bang theory and that the age of the universe is over 10 billion years.

CDFF1180DFE60131985068A86D17958E.description: Understand how knowledge about the universe comes from evidence collected from advanced technology (e.g., telescopes, satellites, images, computer models).

CDFEC100DFE60131984F68A86D17958E.description: Predict changes in the positions and appearances of objects in the sky (e.g., moon, sun) based on knowledge of current positions and patterns of movements (e.g., lunar cycles, seasons).

CDFE7400DFE60131984E68A86D17958E.description:
Understand the scale and contents of the universe, including:
  • range of structures from atoms through astronomical objects to the universe
  • objects in the universe such as planets, stars, galaxies, and nebulae.

CDFE2640DFE60131984D68A86D17958E.description: Examine the scientific theories of the origin, structure, contents, and evolution of the solar system and the universe, and their interconnections.

CDFDD6C0DFE60131984C68A86D17958E.description: (Earth and Space Science): Understand the structure of Earth, the solar system, and the universe, the interconnections among them, and the processes and interactions of Earth's systems.

CDFB0670DFE60131984468A86D17958E.description:
Describe how most cell functions involve chemical reactions, including:
  • promotion or inhibition of biochemical reactions by enzymes
  • processes of respiration (e.g., energy production, ATP)
  • communication from cell to cell by secretion of a variety of chemicals (e.g., hormones).

CDFD8570DFE60131984B68A86D17958E.description: Know that DNA directs protein building (e.g., role of RNA).

CDFD2300DFE60131984A68A86D17958E.description:
Explain how cells differentiate and specialize during the growth of an organism, including:
  • differentiation, regulated through the selected expression of different genes
  • specialized cells, response to stimuli (e.g., nerve cells, sense organs).

CDFCAE30DFE60131984968A86D17958E.description: Know how the cell membrane controls which ions and molecules enter and leave the cell based on membrane permeability and transport (i.e., osmosis, diffusion, active transport, passive transport).

CDFC44C0DFE60131984868A86D17958E.description: Describe the mechanisms for cellular processes (e.g., energy production and storage, transport of molecules, waste disposal, synthesis of new molecules).

CDFBFBC0DFE60131984768A86D17958E.description:
Know that specialized structures inside cells in most organisms carry out different functions, including:
  • parts of a cell and their functions (e.g., nucleus, chromosomes, plasma, and mitochondria)
  • storage of genetic material in DNA
  • similarities and differences between plant and animal cells
  • prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

CDFBAC00DFE60131984668A86D17958E.description: Know that cells are made of proteins composed of combinations of amino acids.

CDFA4280DFE60131984268A86D17958E.description: Understand the characteristics, structures, and functions of cells.

CDF66280DFE60131983768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how evolution by natural selection and other mechanisms explains many phenomena including the fossil record of ancient life forms and similarities (both physical and molecular) among different species.

CDF61690DFE60131983668A86D17958E.description: Explain how natural selection favors individuals who are better able to survive, reproduce, and leave offspring.

CDF5CAC0DFE60131983568A86D17958E.description: Understand that evolution is a consequence of many factors, including the ability of organisms to reproduce, genetic variability, the effect of limited resources, and natural selection.

CDF57D60DFE60131983468A86D17958E.description: Understand the data, observations, and logic supporting the conclusion that species today evolved from earlier, distinctly different species, originating from the ancestral one-celled organisms.

CDF710D0DFE60131983968A86D17958E.description: Critically analyze the data and observations supporting the conclusion that the species living on Earth today are related by descent from the ancestral one-celled organisms.

CDF6C370DFE60131983868A86D17958E.description: Describe the evidence for the first appearance of life on Earth as one-celled organisms, over 3.5 billion years ago, and for the later appearance of a diversity of multicellular organisms over millions of years.

CDF9CC70DFE60131984168A86D17958E.description: Know that most cells in the human body contain 23 pairs of chromosomes including one pair that determines sex, and that human females have two X chromosomes and human males have an X and a Y chromosome.

CDF95930DFE60131984068A86D17958E.description: Understand the principles of sexual and asexual reproduction, including meiosis and mitosis.

CDF90970DFE60131983F68A86D17958E.description:
Know how genetic variability results from the recombination and mutation of genes, including:
  • sorting and recombination of genes in sexual reproduction result in a change in DNA that is passed on to offspring
  • radiation or chemical substances can cause mutations in cells, resulting in a permanent change in DNA.

CDF8BC50DFE60131983E68A86D17958E.description: Identify traits that can and cannot be inherited.

CDF86D00DFE60131983D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the concepts of segregation, independent assortment, and dominant/recessive alleles.

CDF81570DFE60131983C68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate vocabulary to describe inheritable traits (i.e., genotype, phenotype).

CDF7BAF0DFE60131983B68A86D17958E.description:
Know how DNA carries all genetic information in the units of heredity called genes, including:
  • the structure of DNA (e.g., subunits A, G, C, T)
  • information-preserving replication of DNA
  • alteration of genes by inserting, deleting, or substituting parts of DNA.

CDF4DAE0DFE60131983268A86D17958E.description: Understand the genetic basis for inheritance and the basic concepts of biological evolution.

CDF1B0F0DFE60131982868A86D17958E.description:
Understand variation within and among species, including:
  • mutations and genetic drift
  • factors affecting the survival of an organism
  • natural selection.

CDF16460DFE60131982768A86D17958E.description:
Understand and explain the hierarchical classification scheme (i.e., domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species), including:
  • classification of an organism into a category
  • similarity inferred from molecular structure (DNA) closely matching classification based on anatomical similarities
  • similarities of organisms reflecting evolutionary relationships.

CDF2F710DFE60131982C68A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain the principles of photosynthesis (i.e., chloroplasts in plants convert light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into chemical energy).

CDF29BD0DFE60131982B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how energy flows from the sun through plants to herbivores to carnivores and decomposers.

CDF24930DFE60131982A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how matter and energy flow through biological systems (e.g., organisms, communities, ecosystems), and how the total amount of matter and energy is conserved but some energy is always released as heat to the environment.

CDF47340DFE60131983168A86D17958E.description: Critically analyze how humans modify and change ecosystems (e.g., harvesting, pollution, population growth, technology).

CDF427E0DFE60131983068A86D17958E.description: Understand and describe how available resources limit the amount of life an ecosystem can support (e.g., energy, water, oxygen, nutrients).

CDF3DC90DFE60131982F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms cooperate and compete in ecosystems (e.g., producers, decomposers, herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, predator-prey, symbiosis, mutualism).

CDF39100DFE60131982E68A86D17958E.description: Know that an ecosystem is complex and may exhibit fluctuations around a steady state or may evolve over time.

CDF0C290DFE60131982568A86D17958E.description: Understand how the survival of species depends on biodiversity and on complex interactions, including the cycling of matter and the flow of energy.

CDF07520DFE60131982468A86D17958E.description: (Life Science): Understand the properties, structures, and processes of living things and the interdependence of living things and their environments.

CDECDA70DFE60131981968A86D17958E.description: Describe how waves are used for practical purposes (e.g., seismic data, acoustic effects, Doppler effect).

CDEC9180DFE60131981868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the interactions of waves can result in interference, reflection, and refraction.

CDEC46D0DFE60131981768A86D17958E.description: Describe wave propagation using amplitude, wavelength, frequency, and speed.

CDED7D80DFE60131981B68A86D17958E.description: Describe relative motion using frames of reference.

CDED22C0DFE60131981A68A86D17958E.description:
Apply Newton's Laws to describe and analyze the behavior of moving objects, including:
  • displacement, velocity, and acceleration of a moving object
  • Newton's Second Law, F = ma (e.g., momentum and its conservation, the motion of an object falling under gravity, the independence of a falling object's motion on mass)
  • circular motion and centripetal force.

CDF01980DFE60131982368A86D17958E.description: Know that when one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts a force of equal magnitude and in the opposite direction on the first object (i.e., Newton's Third Law).

CDEFC000DFE60131982268A86D17958E.description: Represent the magnitude and direction of forces by vector diagrams.

CDEF60B0DFE60131982168A86D17958E.description: Explain how electric currents cause magnetism and how changing magnetic fields produce electricity (e.g., electric motors, generators).

CDEEFEC0DFE60131982068A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship between force and pressure, and how the pressure of a volume of gas depends on the temperature and the amount of gas.

CDEEAE00DFE60131981F68A86D17958E.description: Know that materials containing equal amounts of positive and negative charges are electrically neutral, but that a small excess or deficit of negative charges produces significant electrical forces.

CDEE60A0DFE60131981E68A86D17958E.description: Know that every object exerts gravitational force on every other object, and how this force depends on the masses of the objects and the distance between them.

CDEE16A0DFE60131981D68A86D17958E.description: Know that there are four fundamental forces in nature: gravitation, electromagnetism, weak nuclear force, and strong nuclear force.

CDEBA720DFE60131981568A86D17958E.description: Understand the motion of objects and waves, and the forces that cause them.

CDE80450DFE60131980A68A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of equilibrium (i.e., thermal, mechanical, and chemical).

CDE7AEA0DFE60131980968A86D17958E.description: Explain how wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation can be used to identify atoms, molecules, and the composition of stars.

CDE8EA80DFE60131980D68A86D17958E.description: Know that each kind of atom or molecule can gain or lose energy only in discrete amounts.

CDE89EE0DFE60131980C68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the characteristics of electromagnetic waves (e.g., visible light, radio, microwave, X-ray, ultraviolet, gamma) and other waves (e.g., sound, seismic waves, water waves), including:
  • origin and potential hazards of various forms of electromagnetic radiation
  • energy of electromagnetic waves carried in discrete energy packets (photons) whose energy is inversely proportional to wavelength.

CDE85480DFE60131980B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that electromagnetic waves carry energy that can be transferred when they interact with matter.

CDEB4BD0DFE60131981468A86D17958E.description: Understand that the ability of energy to do something useful (work) tends to decrease (and never increases) as energy is converted from one form to another.

CDEAF6D0DFE60131981368A86D17958E.description: Explain how heat flows in terms of the transfer of vibrational motion of atoms and molecules from hotter to colder regions.

CDEA9130DFE60131981268A86D17958E.description: Understand how heat can be transferred by conduction, convection, and radiation, and how heat conduction differs in conductors and insulators.

CDEA3F20DFE60131981168A86D17958E.description: Understand that energy can change from one form to another (e.g., changes in kinetic and potential energy in a gravitational field, heats of reaction, hydroelectric dams) and know that energy is conserved in these changes.

CDE9F310DFE60131981068A86D17958E.description: Explain how thermal energy (heat) consists of the random motion and vibrations of atoms and molecules and is measured by temperature.

CDE996D0DFE60131980F68A86D17958E.description: Identify different forms of energy, including kinetic, gravitational (potential), chemical, thermal, nuclear, and electromagnetic.

CDE71570DFE60131980768A86D17958E.description: Understand the transformation and transmission of energy and how energy and matter interact.

CDE28500DFE6013197F968A86D17958E.description: Describe how the rate of chemical reactions depends on many factors that include temperature, concentration, and the presence of catalysts.

CDE22C40DFE6013197F868A86D17958E.description:
Know how to express chemical reactions with balanced equations that show:
  • conservation of mass
  • products of common reactions.

CDE1E380DFE6013197F768A86D17958E.description: Understand types of chemical reactions (e.g., synthesis, decomposition, combustion, redox, neutralization) and identify them as exothermic or endothermic.

CDE19B90DFE6013197F668A86D17958E.description: Know that chemical reactions involve the rearrangement of atoms, and that they occur on many timescales (e.g., picoseconds to millennia).

CDE38730DFE6013197FC68A86D17958E.description:
Know that some atomic nuclei can change, including:
  • spontaneous decay
  • half-life of isotopes
  • fission
  • fusion (e.g., the sun)
  • alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.

CDE33300DFE6013197FB68A86D17958E.description: Know that states of matter (i.e., solid, liquid, gas) depend on the arrangement of atoms and molecules and on their freedom of motion.

CDE518E0DFE60131980168A86D17958E.description: Understand how the type and arrangement of atoms and their bonds determine macroscopic properties (e.g., boiling point, electrical conductivity, hardness of minerals).

CDE4D030DFE60131980068A86D17958E.description: Make predictions about elements using the periodic table (e.g., number of valence electrons, metallic character, reactivity, conductivity, type of bond between elements).

CDE48560DFE6013197FF68A86D17958E.description:
Explain how electrons determine the properties of substances by:
  • interactions between atoms through transferring or sharing valence electrons
  • ionic and covalent bonds
  • the ability of carbon to form a diverse array of organic structures

CDE43720DFE6013197FE68A86D17958E.description:
Understand atomic structure, including:
  • most space occupied by electrons
  • nucleus made of protons and neutrons
  • isotopes of an element
  • masses of proton and neutron 2000 times greater than mass of electron
  • atom held together by proton-electron electrical forces.

CDE3DF20DFE6013197FD68A86D17958E.description: Understand that matter is made of atoms and that atoms are made of subatomic particles.

CDE6C7B0DFE60131980668A86D17958E.description: Describe trends in properties (e.g., ionization energy or reactivity as a function of location on the periodic table, boiling point of organic liquids as a function of molecular weight).

CDE67770DFE60131980568A86D17958E.description: Know how to use properties to separate mixtures into pure substances (e.g., distillation, chromatography, solubility).

CDE61C30DFE60131980468A86D17958E.description: Identify, measure, and use a variety of physical and chemical properties (e.g., electrical conductivity, density, viscosity, chemical reactivity, pH, melting point).

CDE5BA60DFE60131980368A86D17958E.description: Classify matter in a variety of ways (e.g., element, compound, mixture; solid, liquid, gas; acidic, basic, neutral).

CDE0FAC0DFE6013197F468A86D17958E.description: Understand the properties, underlying structure, and reactions of matter.

CDE0A6D0DFE6013197F368A86D17958E.description: (Physical Science): Understand the structure and properties of matter, the characteristics of energy, and the interactions between matter and energy.

CDDFFAC0DFE6013197F168A86D17958E.description: Use mathematics to express and establish scientific relationships (e.g., scientific notation, vectors, dimensional analysis).

CDDFB160DFE6013197F068A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply measurement techniques and consider possible effects of measurement errors.

CDDF67D0DFE6013197EF68A86D17958E.description: Use technologies to quantify relationships in scientific hypotheses (e.g., calculators, computer spreadsheets and databases, graphing software, simulations, modeling).

CDDF1D20DFE6013197EE68A86D17958E.description: Use mathematical models to describe, explain, and predict natural phenomena.

CDDECDC0DFE6013197ED68A86D17958E.description: Create multiple displays of data to analyze and explain the relationships in scientific investigations.

CDDE7980DFE6013197EC68A86D17958E.description: Students will use mathematical concepts, principles, and expressions to analyze data, develop models, understand patterns and relationships, evaluate findings, and draw conclusions.

CDDE27F0DFE6013197EB68A86D17958E.description: Examine the scientific processes and logic used in investigations of past events (e.g., using data from crime scenes, fossils), investigations that can be planned in advance but are only done once (e.g., expensive or time-consuming experiments such as medical clinical trials), and investigations of phenomena that can be repeated easily and frequently.

CDDDBD60DFE6013197EA68A86D17958E.description: Examine investigations of current interest in science (e.g., superconductivity, molecular machines, age of the universe).

CDDD6310DFE6013197E968A86D17958E.description: Critically analyze an accepted explanation by reviewing current scientific knowledge.

CDDD1100DFE6013197E868A86D17958E.description: Understand how new data and observations can result in new scientific knowledge.

CDDCB4B0DFE6013197E768A86D17958E.description:
Use scientific reasoning and valid logic to recognize:
  • faulty logic
  • cause and effect
  • the difference between observation and unsubstantiated inferences and conclusions
  • potential bias.

CDDC6C00DFE6013197E668A86D17958E.description:
Understand how scientific processes produce valid, reliable results, including:
  • consistency of explanations with data and observations
  • openness to peer review
  • full disclosure and examination of assumptions
  • testability of hypotheses
  • repeatability of experiments and reproducibility of results.

CDDC22B0DFE6013197E568A86D17958E.description: Students will understand that scientific processes produce scientific knowledge that is continually evaluated, validated, revised, or rejected.

CDDBD910DFE6013197E468A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific theories are used to explain and predict natural phenomena (e.g., plate tectonics, ocean currents, structure of atom).

CDDB8C00DFE6013197E368A86D17958E.description:
Convey results of investigations using scientific concepts, methodologies, and expressions, including:
  • scientific language and symbols
  • diagrams, charts, and other data displays
  • mathematical expressions and processes (e.g., mean, median, slope, proportionality)
  • clear, logical, and concise communication
  • reasoned arguments.

CDDAD940DFE6013197E168A86D17958E.description:
Design and conduct scientific investigations that include:
  • testable hypotheses
  • controls and variables
  • methods to collect, analyze, and interpret data
  • results that address hypotheses being investigated
  • predictions based on results
  • re-evaluation of hypotheses and additional experimentation as necessary
  • error analysis.

CDDB34A0DFE6013197E268A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate technologies to collect, analyze, and communicate scientific data (e.g., computers, calculators, balances, microscopes).

CDDA84B0DFE6013197E068A86D17958E.description: Describe the essential components of an investigation, including appropriate methodologies, proper equipment, and safety precautions.

CDDA2DF0DFE6013197DF68A86D17958E.description: Students will use accepted scientific methods to collect, analyze, and interpret data and observations and to design and conduct scientific investigations and communicate results.

CDD9D5F0DFE6013197DE68A86D17958E.description: Understand the processes of scientific investigations and use inquiry and scientific ways of observing, experimenting, predicting, and validating to think critically.

document.title: Social Studies K-4 Content Standards with Benchmarks and Performance Standards

C9A23490DFE601318F8668A86D17958E.description: Understand that money is the generally accepted medium of exchange in most societies, and that different countries use different currencies.

C9A1F4C0DFE601318F8568A86D17958E.description: Understand the patterns and results of trade and exchange among individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies, and their interdependent qualities.

C9A1B450DFE601318F8468A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of the worker in the local economy.

C9A172A0DFE601318F8368A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles of producers and consumers in the production of goods and services.

C9A12BE0DFE601318F8268A86D17958E.description: Understand that economic systems impact the way individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies make decisions about goods and services.

C9A0DD40DFE601318F8168A86D17958E.description: Identify economic decisions made by individuals and households and explain how resources are distributed.

C9A098F0DFE601318F8068A86D17958E.description: Understand that individuals, households, businesses, governments, and societies make decisions that affect the distribution of resources and that these decisions are influenced by incentives (both economic and intrinsic).

C9A052E0DFE601318F7F68A86D17958E.description: Students understand basic economic principles and use economic reasoning skills to analyze the impact of economic systems (including the market economy) on individuals, families, businesses, communities, and governments.

C99EF040DFE601318F7B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the responsibilities of being a member of various groups (e.g. family, school, community).

C99EA5F0DFE601318F7A68A86D17958E.description: Understand characteristics of "good citizenship" as exemplified by historic and ordinary people.

C99E6020DFE601318F7968A86D17958E.description: Understand rights and responsibilities of "good citizenship" as members of a family, school and community.

C99FA0D0DFE601318F7D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the concept of "public good" and identify local examples of systems that support the "public good."

C99F4D10DFE601318F7C68A86D17958E.description: Become familiar with the basic purposes of government in New Mexico and the United States.

C99E0CD0DFE601318F7868A86D17958E.description: Identify local governing officials and explain how their roles reflect their community.

C99DA380DFE601318F7768A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the symbols, icons, songs, traditions, and leaders of local, state, tribal, and national levels that exemplify ideals and provide continuity and a sense of community across time.

C99D52B0DFE601318F7668A86D17958E.description: Describe and compare class rules made by direct democracy (entire class votes on the rules) and by representative democracy (class elects a smaller group to make the rules).

C99CC7A0DFE601318F7468A86D17958E.description: Know the fundamental purposes, concepts, structures, and functions of local, state, tribal, and national governments.

C99C8670DFE601318F7368A86D17958E.description: Students understand the ideals, rights, and responsibilities of citizenship and understand the content and history of the founding documents of the United States with particular emphasis on the United States and New Mexico constitutions and how governments function at local, state, tribal, and national levels.

C99B8270DFE601318F6F68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that people and groups can conserve and replenish natural resources.

C99B3AA0DFE601318F6E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how natural and man-made changes affect the meaning, use, distribution, and value of resources.

C99A6A40DFE601318F6B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how characteristics of culture affect behaviors and lifestyles.

C99A18E0DFE601318F6A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how economic, political, cultural, and social processes interact to shape patterns of human populations, and their interdependence, cooperation, and conflict.

C999C8C0DFE601318F6968A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics of physical systems (e.g., water cycle).

C9996FF0DFE601318F6868A86D17958E.description: Describe the physical processes that affect the Earth's features (e.g., weather, erosion).

C99930E0DFE601318F6768A86D17958E.description: Understand how physical processes shape the Earth's surface patterns and biosystems.

C9980190DFE601318F6368A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which people depend on natural and man-made environments including natural resources to meet basic needs.

C997AA60DFE601318F6268A86D17958E.description: Be familiar with aspects of human behavior and man-made and natural environments in order to recognize their impact on the past and present.

C9976990DFE601318F6168A86D17958E.description: Explain how people depend on the environment and its resources to satisfy their basic needs.

C9972840DFE601318F6068A86D17958E.description: Describe how climate, natural resources, and natural hazards affect activities and settlement patterns.

C996E510DFE601318F5F68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between natural and human characteristics of places and use this knowledge to define regions, their relationships with other regions, and patterns of change.

  3. impact of population changes (e.g., population growth, rural-to-urban migrations, growth of industrial cities, emigration out of Europe)
  4. evolution of work/business and the role of labor (e.g., the demise of slavery, division of labor, union movement, impact of immigration)
  5. political and economic theories of capitalism and socialism (e.g., Adam Smith, Karl Marx)
  6. status and roles of women and minorities

  1. Copernican view of the universe and Newton's natural laws
  2. tension and cooperation between religion and new scientific discoveries
  3. impact of Galileo's ideas and the introduction of the scientific method as a means of understanding the universe
  4. events and ideas that led to parliamentary government (English civil war, glorious revolution)
  5. enlightenment philosophies used to support events leading to American and French revolutions
  6. Napoleonic era (e.g., codification of law); Latin America's wars of independence

  1. development of renaissance artistic and literary traditions (e.g., Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, Shakespeare)
  2. development of protestantism (e.g., Martin Luther, John Calvin)
  3. religious conflict and persecutions (e.g., Spanish inquisition)

  1. analyze perspectives that have shaped the structures of historical knowledge
  2. describe ways historians study the past
  3. explain connections made between the past and the present and their impact

C8F76700DFE601318E4D68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the impact of the post-cold war Era on United States' foreign policy, to include:
  1. role of the United States in supporting democracy in eastern Europe following the collapse of the Berlin wall
  2. new allegiances in defining the new world order
  3. role of technology in the information age

C8F70590DFE601318E4C68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the impact of World War II and the cold war on United States' foreign and domestic policy, to include:
  1. origins, dynamics and consequences of the cold war tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union
  2. new role of the United States as a world leader (e.g., Marshall plan, NATO)
  3. need for, establishment and support of the united nations
  4. implementation of the foreign policy of containment, including the Truman doctrine
  5. Red Scare (e.g., McCarthyism, House Un-American Activities Committee, nuclear weapons, arms race)
  6. external confrontations with communism (e.g., the Berlin blockade, Berlin wall, Bay of Pigs, Cuban missile crisis, Korea, Vietnam war)
  7. Sputnik and the space race
  8. image of 1950s affluent society
  9. political protests of Vietnam war)
  10. counterculture in the 1960s

C8F6AC20DFE601318E4B68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the development of voting and civil rights for all groups in the United States following reconstruction, to include:
  1. intent and impact of the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments to the constitution
  2. segregation as enforced by Jim Crow laws following reconstruction
  3. key court cases (e.g., Plessy v. Ferguson, Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Roe v. Wade)
  4. roles and methods of civil rights advocates (e.g., Martin Luther King, Jr., Malcolm X, Rosa Parks, Russell Means, César Chávez)
  5. the passage and effect of the voting rights legislation on minorities (e.g., 19th amendment, role of Arizona supreme court decision on Native Americans, their disenfranchisement under Arizona constitution and subsequent changes made in other state constitutions regarding Native American voting rights - such as New Mexico, 1962, 1964 Civil Rights Act, Voting Act of 1965, 24th Amendment)
  6. impact and reaction to the efforts to pass the Equal Rights Amendment
  7. rise of black power, brown power, American Indian movement, united farm workers

  2. events on the home front to support the war effort (e.g., war bond drives, mobilization of the war industry, women and minorities in the work force)
  3. major turning points in the war (e.g., the battle of Midway, D-Day invasion, dropping of atomic bombs on Japan)

  2. causes of the great depression (e.g., over production, under consumption, credit structure)
  3. rise of youth culture in the "jazz age"
  4. development of mass/popular culture (e.g., rise of radio, movies, professional sports, popular literature)
  5. human and natural crises of the great depression, (e.g., unemployment, food lines, the dust bowl, western migration of midwest farmers)

  7. role of changing demographics on traditional communities and social structures

  1. causes for a change in foreign policy from isolationism to interventionism; causes and consequences of the Spanish American war
  2. expanding influence in the western hemisphere (e.g., the Panama canal, Roosevelt corollary added to the Monroe doctrine, the "big stick" policy, "dollar diplomacy")
  3. events that led to the United States' involvement in World War I; United States' rationale for entry into World War I and impact on military process, public opinion and policy
  4. United States' mobilization in World War I (e.g., its impact on politics, economics and society)

  3. development of monopolies and their impact on economic and political policies (e.g., laissez-faire economics, trusts, trust busting)
  4. growth of cities (e.g., influx of immigrants, rural-to-urban migrations, racial and ethnic conflicts that resulted)
  5. efforts of workers to improve working conditions (e.g., organizing labor unions, strikes, strike breakers)
  6. rise and effect of reform movements (e.g., Populists, William Jennings Bryan, Jane Addams, muckrakers)
  7. conservation of natural resources (e.g., the Grand Canyon, Yellowstone, Anasazi ruins at Mesa Verde, Colorado, National Reclamation Act of 1902)
  8. progressive reforms (e.g., the national income tax, direct election of senators, women's suffrage, prohibition)

  2. development of concepts of government and citizenship (e.g., democracy, republic, codification of laws, Code of Hammurabi)
  3. scientific and cultural advancements (e.g., networks of roads, aqueducts, art, architecture, literature, theater, philosophy)

  2. life of Confucius and the fundamental teachings of Confucianism and Taoism
  3. rule by dynasties (e.g., Shang, Qin, Han, Tang, and Ming)
  4. historical influence of China on other parts of the world (e.g., tea, paper, wood-block printing, compass, gunpowder)

  4. key historical figures
  5. religious traditions, cultural, and scientific contributions (e.g., writing systems, calendars, building of monuments such as the pyramids)

  1. reconstruction plans; impact of Lincoln's assassination and the impeachment of Andrew Johnson
  2. attempts to protect the rights and enhance the opportunities for freedmen by the 13th, 14th and 15th amendments to the United States constitution
  3. post-civil war segregation policies and their resulting impact on racial issues in the United States

CA3B4860DFE60131910768A86D17958E.description:

  1. contributions and significance of key figures (e.g., Abraham Lincoln, Jefferson Davis, Robert E. Lee, William Tecumseh Sherman, Ulysses S. Grant)
  2. major turning points in the civil war, including Gettysburg; unique nature of the civil war (e.g., impact of Americans fighting Americans, high casualties caused by disease and type of warfare, widespread destruction of American property)
  3. role of African Americans; purpose and effect of the emancipation proclamation

  1. different economies that developed in the north, south and west; addition of new states to the union and the balance of power in the United States senate (Missouri and 1850 compromises)
  2. extension of slavery into the territories (e.g., Dred Scott decision, Kansas-Nebraska Act, Frederick Douglass, John Brown)
  3. presidential election of 1860, Lincoln's victory and the south's secession

CA3AA920DFE60131910568A86D17958E.description:

  3. origins and early history of the women's movement

  2. creation of political parties (democratic republicans and the federalists)

CA39E1D0DFE60131910268A86D17958E.description:

  2. major debates of the constitutional convention and their resolution (e.g., the federalist papers), contributions and roles of major individuals in the writing and ratification of the constitution (e.g., George Washington, James Madison, Alexander Hamilton, Thomas Jefferson, James Monroe, John Jay)
  3. struggles over ratification of the constitution and the creation of the bill of rights

document.title: Science Content Standards, Benchmarks, and Performance Standards

CDA358C0DFE60131978C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how scientific information can help individuals and communities respond to health emergencies (e.g., CPR, epidemics, HIV, bio-terrorism).

CDA30800DFE60131978B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how technologies have been responsible for advances in medicine (e.g., vaccines, antibiotics, microscopes, DNA technologies).

CDA2C190DFE60131978A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the contributions of science to health as they relate to personal decisions about smoking, drugs, alcohol, and sexual activity.

CDA28130DFE60131978968A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific discoveries and inventions have changed individuals and societies.

CDA23FF0DFE60131978868A86D17958E.description: Understand how scientific discoveries, inventions, practices, and knowledge influence, and are influenced by, individuals and societies.

CDA199C0DFE60131978668A86D17958E.description: Know that changes to ecosystems sometimes decrease the capacity of the environment to support some life forms and are difficult and/or costly to remediate.

CDA14480DFE60131978568A86D17958E.description: Understand how living organisms have played many roles in changes of Earth's systems through time (e.g., atmospheric composition, creation of soil, impact on Earth's surface).

CDA10000DFE60131978468A86D17958E.description:
Understand how the remains of living things give us information about the history of Earth, including:

CDA0BA80DFE60131978368A86D17958E.description: Describe the structure of Earth and its atmosphere and explain how energy, matter, and forces shape Earth's systems.

CDA077A0DFE60131978268A86D17958E.description: Explain how energy from the sun supports life on Earth.

CDA034F0DFE60131978168A86D17958E.description: Explain why Earth is unique in our solar system in its ability to support life.

CD9FE910DFE60131978068A86D17958E.description: Describe how the concepts of energy, matter, and force can be used to explain the observed behavior of the solar system, the universe, and their structures.

CD9F9A60DFE60131977F68A86D17958E.description: (Earth and Space Science): Understand the structure of Earth, the solar system, and the universe, the interconnections among them, and the processes and interactions of Earth's systems.

CD9E4650DFE60131977B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how factors (radiation, UV light, drugs) can damage cellular structure or function.

CD9DFAE0DFE60131977A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how some cells respond to stimuli (e.g., light, heat, pressure, gravity).

CD9DB520DFE60131977968A86D17958E.description: Compare the structure and processes of plant cells and animal cells.

CD9D5150DFE60131977868A86D17958E.description:

CD9F54A0DFE60131977E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how organs are composed of tissues of different types of cells (e.g., skin, bone, muscle, heart, intestines).

CD9F0B10DFE60131977D68A86D17958E.description: Understand that organisms are composed of cells and identify unicellular and multicellular organisms.

CD9CA290DFE60131977668A86D17958E.description: Understand the structure of organisms and the function of cells in living systems.

CD992FE0DFE60131976A68A86D17958E.description: Know that the fossil record documents the appearance, diversification, and extinction of many life forms.

CD98CEC0DFE60131976968A86D17958E.description: Explain how species adapt to changes in the environment or become extinct and that extinction of species is common in the history of living things.

CD988870DFE60131976868A86D17958E.description: Understand the process of natural selection.

CD983A40DFE60131976768A86D17958E.description: Identify adaptations that favor the survival of organisms in their environments (e.g., camouflage, shape of beak).

CD9A2980DFE60131976D68A86D17958E.description: Know that organisms can acquire unique characteristics through naturally occurring genetic variations.

CD99D570DFE60131976C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that diversity within a species is developed by gradual changes over many generations.

CD998650DFE60131976B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how typical traits may change from generation to generation due to environmental influences (e.g., color of skin, shape of eyes, camouflage, shape of beak).

CD9AAF60DFE60131976F68A86D17958E.description: Understand that some characteristics are passed from parent to offspring as inherited traits and others are acquired from interactions with the environment.

CD96FDF0DFE60131976368A86D17958E.description: Explain the conditions and resources needed to sustain life in specific ecosystems.

CD9463F0DFE60131975A68A86D17958E.description: (Life Science): Understand the properties, structures, and processes of living things and the interdependence of living things and their environments.

CD940CB0DFE60131975968A86D17958E.description:

CD93BD60DFE60131975868A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain forces that produce motion in objects.

CD936A00DFE60131975768A86D17958E.description:
Know how various forms of energy are transformed through organisms and ecosystems, including:

  • effect of mankind's use of energy and other activities on living systems (e.g., global warming, water quality).

CD932760DFE60131975668A86D17958E.description: Explain the physical processes involved in the transfer, change, and conservation of energy.

CD92E560DFE60131975568A86D17958E.description: Know that chemical reactions are essential to life processes.

CD91FB70DFE60131975268A86D17958E.description: Know that the total amount of matter (mass) remains constant although its form, location, and properties may change (e.g., matter in the food web).

CD91B060DFE60131975168A86D17958E.description: Explain how matter is transferred from one organism to another and between organisms and their environment (e.g., consumption, the water cycle, the carbon cycle, the nitrogen cycle).

CD9170D0DFE60131975068A86D17958E.description: Know the forms and properties of matter and how matter interacts.

CD912FC0DFE60131974F68A86D17958E.description: (Physical Science): Understand the structure and properties of matter, the characteristics of energy, and the interactions between matter and energy.

CD90AB00DFE60131974D68A86D17958E.description: Select and use an appropriate model to examine a phenomenon.

CD8F3480DFE60131974868A86D17958E.description: Critique procedures used to investigate a hypothesis.
